# **Read this first**

You have four working days. That is not enough time to build something impressive, so we are not going to try. We are going to build something that works end to end and is honest about its limits — which is harder, more useful, and far more interesting to demo.

**The three rules of this sprint**

1\. Working beats clever. A crude stage that runs is worth more than an elegant one that does not.

2\. Nobody waits for anybody. The sample data file exists from Monday evening. If you are blocked on a teammate, you are using the sample file wrong.

3\. Thursday 9pm is a feature freeze. After that you fix bugs and write documentation. Nothing new gets added.

## **What you are building**

A pipeline that takes one business category in one city, finds 100 real businesses, audits their websites, researches each one, scores them, drafts a personalised email for the best ones, and puts them in front of a human to approve — after which the message goes to a test inbox.

It is a genuinely small version of what Logitrix does by hand. That is the point: at the end you will have built something the agency could actually use, not a tutorial project.

# **1\. How the project flows**

Seven people, one straight line. Each stage reads the file the previous stage wrote, adds its own fields, and writes a new file. There are no APIs between stages and no database — in four days, files are faster to build and far easier to debug.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 1 — The pipeline, with who owns each stage and what file they produce_

**Why files instead of services**

When a stage breaks, you can open the file and look at it. When a service breaks, you are reading logs at 1am.

It also means every stage can be re-run on its own without restarting anything, which is exactly what you need when you are debugging under time pressure.

# **2\. The shared data format**

This is the single thing that makes seven people's work fit together. Haseeb publishes it on Monday. After that it changes only by telling everyone in the group chat first.

Each stage reads a JSONL file — one JSON object per line — and writes a new one with extra fields added. Nothing is ever removed.

## **The record after every stage has run**

{

"lead_id": "sd_0042", // Stage 1 — Nurul

"name": "Coastal Realty Group",

"domain": "coastalrealtygroup.com",

"city": "San Diego",

"category": "real_estate_agency",

"phone": "+1-619-555-0142",

"site_text": "Coastal Realty Group has served...",

"visual_ok": true, // Stage 2 — Intern 5

"screenshot_desktop": "screenshots/sd_0042_d.png",

"screenshot_mobile": "screenshots/sd_0042_m.png",

"has_contact_method": false,

"loads_under_5s": true,

"mobile_friendly": false,

"has_meta_description": false,

"findings": \[ // Stage 3 — Haseeb

{ "claim": "No contact form on any page",

"quote": "Call us during office hours",

"category": "conversion",

"quote_verified": true }

\],

"score": 78, // Stage 4 — Azlan

"band": "A",

"score_reasons": \["no contact method", "not mobile friendly", "no meta description"\],

"subject": "Quick note about your mobile site", // Stage 5 — Amna

"body": "Hi Coastal Realty team — I noticed...",

"claims_referenced": 2,

"decision": "approve", // Dashboard — Umer

"final_body": "Hi Coastal Realty team — ...",

"decided_at": "2026-08-24T19:14:02Z"

}

**The one rule that protects everyone**

Copy every field you received through to your output, then add yours. Never drop a field because you do not use it — someone downstream does.

# **Nurul Huda — Collect the leads**

**STAGE 1 Output file: data/01_leads.jsonl**

**Why your piece matters**

Nothing downstream exists until this file does. Six people are waiting on the shape and quality of your output, which makes you the most time-critical person on Tuesday morning.

## **What you actually do**

- Query the Overpass API for one business category in one city — target 120 results so you end with 100 usable ones.
- For each business that has a website, fetch the homepage and the About or Services page.
- Strip the HTML down to readable text with trafilatura. Cap it at 4,000 characters so the LLM stages stay inside the free tier.
- Drop businesses with no website at all — they cannot be audited, so they are not leads for this project.
- Merge obvious duplicates on domain, then on fuzzy name match.
- Write one JSON object per line to data/01_leads.jsonl.

## **Your tech stack**

Python 3.11 · requests or httpx · trafilatura · rapidfuzz · json

## **Day by day**

| **Day** | **Your goal**                                                                                       |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mon     | Attend kickoff. Get the Overpass query returning results in your terminal. Nothing else.            |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                 |
| Tue     | Collector script working end to end on 20 businesses. Commit it.                                    |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                 |
| Wed     | Run 120 businesses, clean, dedupe, hand the real file to the team by 2pm.                           |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                 |
| Thu     | Fix whatever the downstream stages complain about. Add a --limit flag so others can test on 5 rows. |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                 |
| Fri     | Two-minute demo slot: show the raw source and the cleaned record side by side.                      |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                 |

## **You are done when**

1. data/01_leads.jsonl has 100+ lines
2. Every line has lead_id, name, domain, city, site_text
3. No two lines share a domain
4. The script runs from the command line with a --limit flag

## **What this teaches you**

Working with a real public API, handling HTML that fights back, and the discipline of writing a file other people build against.

# **Intern 5 — Look at the website**

**STAGE 2 Output file: data/02_visual.jsonl**

**Why your piece matters**

You produce the evidence that makes the outreach specific. "Your site has no contact form on mobile" is a sales hook; "your site could be better" is not.

## **What you actually do**

- Open each lead's website with Playwright and screenshot it at desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px).
- Save both images into screenshots/ named by lead_id.
- Run four checks that need no model at all: is there a visible phone number or contact form, does the page load in under 5 seconds, does the mobile view need horizontal scrolling, does the page have a title and meta description.
- Optional and only if Tuesday goes well: run pre-trained YOLOv8 inference on the screenshots to count detected UI elements. Inference only — there is no time to train anything, and that is fine.
- Copy every input field through and add your new fields.

## **Your tech stack**

Python 3.11 · Playwright · Pillow · (optional) Ultralytics YOLOv8 pre-trained weights

## **Day by day**

| **Day** | **Your goal**                                                                                                                          |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mon     | Install Playwright and successfully screenshot one website. That is the whole Monday goal.                                             |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                    |
| Tue     | Screenshot loop plus the four checks, running on the 10 sample rows.                                                                   |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                    |
| Wed     | Run on the 20 real leads. Handle sites that hang or block you — a failure must write a row with visual_ok: false, never crash the run. |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                    |
| Thu     | Run all 100. Optional YOLO inference if you are ahead.                                                                                 |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                    |
| Fri     | Two-minute demo: show a good site and a bad site side by side with their check results.                                                |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                    |

## **You are done when**

1. Screenshots exist for 90+ of the 100 leads
2. Every lead has all four check results, even failures
3. A blocked site produces a row, not a crash
4. Someone else can run your script with one command

## **What this teaches you**

Browser automation, building a dataset of real screenshots, and the engineering lesson that rule-based checks often beat a model when time is short.

# **Haseeb Khan — Research each business**

**STAGE 3 Output file: data/03_research.jsonl**

**Why your piece matters**

You turn raw page text into three specific, quotable findings per lead. You are also the technical lead for this sprint: you own the record format and you open and close the demo.

## **What you actually do**

- Day 0, before anything else: publish contracts/lead_schema.json and commit data/sample_10.jsonl with ten realistic fake leads. Six people are blocked until this exists — it is due Monday, not Tuesday.
- For each lead, send the site text plus the visual check results to the LLM and ask for exactly three findings.
- Force structured output: each finding must have a claim, a supporting quote from the site text, and a category (design, content, conversion or trust).
- Reject any finding whose quote does not literally appear in the site text. This check is 15 lines of Python and it is the most valuable thing you will build this week.
- Cap it at one LLM call per lead so the free tier survives 100 leads.

## **Your tech stack**

Python 3.11 · LangChain or the Gemini SDK directly · Pydantic for structured output · Gemini free tier, Groq as backup

## **Day by day**

| **Day** | **Your goal**                                                                                                                                  |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mon     | Publish the schema and the sample file by 6pm. Run the kickoff. This is your only Monday job and it is not optional.                           |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                            |
| Tue     | Prompt written, structured output parsing working, first three findings generated for a sample lead.                                           |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                            |
| Wed     | Add the quote-verification check. Run on the 20 real leads and report what percentage of findings survive verification.                        |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                            |
| Thu     | Run all 100. Help Intern 5 and Amna if they are behind — that is part of your role, not a favour.                                              |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                            |
| Fri     | Open the demo with a two-minute architecture walkthrough, then close it with what you would do next. No code on screen during the walkthrough. |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                                            |

## **You are done when**

1. Schema and sample file committed on Monday
2. Every lead has exactly 3 findings
3. Every finding's quote is verified to exist in the source text
4. You can state the verification pass rate as a number
5. You presented twice on Friday without opening an editor

## **What this teaches you**

Structured LLM output, grounding verification, and the part that will feel least natural: writing something six other people build against, and explaining it out loud.

# **Azlan — Score the leads**

**STAGE 4 Output file: data/04_scored.jsonl**

**Why your piece matters**

You decide who gets contacted first. With no historical outcomes there is nothing to train on, so you build a transparent scorecard — and then prove it agrees with human judgement.

## **What you actually do**

- Design a weighted scorecard from signals the earlier stages produced: number of failed visual checks, whether findings are conversion-related, presence of contact details, site text length, category match.
- Output an integer 0 to 100 plus a band: A is 75+, B is 50 to 74, C is 25 to 49, D is below 25.
- Output score_reasons — the three signals that contributed most — so the dashboard can show why.
- Validation, and this is the real work: have three teammates independently rank 20 leads best to worst. Compare your ranking to theirs with Spearman correlation. Report the number honestly, including if it is bad.
- Because you will finish early: you are also the repo owner. Set up the folder structure, the shared requirements.txt, and the .env.example on Monday.

## **Your tech stack**

Python 3.11 · pandas · scipy for the correlation · no ML framework needed, and resisting the urge to add one is part of the exercise

## **Day by day**

| **Day** | **Your goal**                                                                                            |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mon     | Set up the repo skeleton and requirements.txt for everyone. Push it before the kickoff ends.             |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                      |
| Tue     | Scorecard implemented and running on the sample file. Send the 20-lead ranking sheet to three teammates. |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                      |
| Wed     | Run on real leads. Compute the correlation against human ranking. Tune the weights once, then stop.      |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                      |
| Thu     | Run all 100. Write a half-page note on what the scorecard cannot see and what data would fix it.         |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                      |
| Fri     | Two-minute demo: your weights, your correlation number, and one lead the scorecard got wrong.            |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                      |

## **You are done when**

1. Every lead has a score, a band and three reasons
2. Spearman correlation against human ranking is computed and stated
3. The repo skeleton was ready on Monday
4. The half-page limitations note exists

## **What this teaches you**

Building a defensible model with no labels, validating against human judgement instead of a metric, and the discipline of not reaching for XGBoost when a scorecard is the right answer.

# **Amna Miraj — Write the message**

**STAGE 5 Output file: data/05_drafts.jsonl**

**Why your piece matters**

Everything upstream exists to make your email specific. If your draft could have been sent to any business in the list, the whole pipeline was pointless.

## **What you actually do**

- Build a prompt that takes the business name, the three findings and the score band, and produces a subject line plus a body under 120 words.
- Require the body to reference at least two findings by their specific content — not "your website has issues" but the actual thing.
- Force structured output so you get subject and body as separate fields, never one blob of text.
- Write a checker: for each draft, confirm that at least two finding claims are recognisably present in the body. Flag drafts that fail.
- Score 10 drafts by hand on a 1 to 5 scale for specificity and tone. Publish the average.
- Only generate for bands A and B — C and D leads get no draft. This saves quota and mirrors how it would work in reality.

## **Your tech stack**

Python 3.11 · Gemini free tier with Groq fallback · Pydantic for structured output

## **Day by day**

| **Day** | **Your goal**                                                                                        |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mon     | Get one LLM API call returning text from your machine. That is the Monday goal.                      |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                  |
| Tue     | Prompt written, structured output working, first drafts generated from the sample findings.          |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                  |
| Wed     | Add the two-findings checker. Generate for the real A and B leads.                                   |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                  |
| Thu     | Generate all. Hand-score 10, publish the average, rewrite the prompt once if the average is under 3. |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                  |
| Fri     | Two-minute demo: read one strong draft aloud, then one weak one, and say what made the difference.   |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                  |

## **You are done when**

1. Every A and B lead has a subject and a body under 120 words
2. The two-findings check runs and flags failures
3. 10 drafts hand-scored with the average published
4. No draft invents a fact that is not in the findings

## **What this teaches you**

Prompt engineering with real inputs, structured output, and evaluating generated text when there is no accuracy metric to hide behind.

# **Mian Usman — Run and deliver**

**RUNNER Output file: run_pipeline.py + n8n**

**Why your piece matters**

Five scripts run by five people on five laptops is not a product. You make it one command — and you are the one who finds the integration bugs, because you are the only person who runs everything in sequence.

## **What you actually do**

- Write run_pipeline.py that calls all five stages in order, prints how many rows each stage read and wrote, and stops with a clear message if a stage produces zero rows.
- Wrap it in an n8n workflow with a schedule trigger and a failure branch that posts to the team chat.
- Write send_approved.py: read data/06_approved.jsonl, send each message through Mailtrap, and record delivery status. Mailtrap only — no real mail credentials exist anywhere in this repo.
- Build a suppression list: any lead marked rejected is never sent, even if it reappears in a later run.
- From Wednesday onward you run the full pipeline every evening and report to the team what broke. That report is your most valuable output.

## **Your tech stack**

Python 3.11 · subprocess or direct imports · n8n self-hosted in Docker · Mailtrap sandbox SMTP

## **Day by day**

| **Day** | **Your goal**                                                                                                            |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Mon     | Get n8n running in Docker and confirm you can open it in a browser. Create the Mailtrap inbox and share credentials.     |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                      |
| Tue     | Write run_pipeline.py against the sample file, even though the real stages are half-built. Stub what does not exist yet. |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                      |
| Wed     | First real end-to-end run. Report every failure to the team by 9pm — this is Check 2.                                    |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                      |
| Thu     | n8n wrapper, send_approved.py, suppression list. Send 10 approved drafts to the sandbox and screenshot the inbox.        |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                      |
| Fri     | Two-minute demo: run the whole pipeline live from one command, then show the sandbox inbox.                              |
| ---     | ---                                                                                                                      |

## **You are done when**

1. python run_pipeline.py runs all five stages from a clean checkout
2. Row counts print between every stage
3. n8n triggers it on a schedule
4. 10 approved messages visible in the Mailtrap inbox
5. A rejected lead is provably never sent

## **What this teaches you**

Integration is a skill, not an afterthought. Also: n8n moving data around a Python pipeline, which is exactly how this works in real agencies.

Test small. Run big once. If you burn the shared quota on Tuesday, the team loses Wednesday.

# **6\. Rules that do not bend**

| **Rule**                                                              | **Why**                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No message is sent to a real business. Mailtrap only.                 | This is training data collection, not a live campaign. Real mail credentials never enter this repository.         |
| ---                                                                   | ---                                                                                                               |
| Only public business information. No personal data about individuals. | Business name, business address, business phone, business website. Nothing about a person.                        |
| ---                                                                   | ---                                                                                                               |
| Respect robots.txt and go slow — one request per second per site.     | You are crawling real companies. Getting the team's IP blocked on Tuesday ends the sprint.                        |
| ---                                                                   | ---                                                                                                               |
| Identify your crawler in the user agent.                              | It costs nothing and it is the difference between a research crawler and a nuisance.                              |
| ---                                                                   | ---                                                                                                               |
| Never invent a fact about a business.                                 | If the site does not say it, it does not go in a finding or an email. This is what the quote verification is for. |
| ---                                                                   | ---                                                                                                               |

# **7\. If you fall behind**

You will fall behind somewhere. That is expected in a four-day sprint and it is not a failure — pretending it is not happening is. Cut in this order, and tell the group chat when you cut.

| **Cut this first**                                                | **Then this**                                       | **Never cut this**                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| YOLO inference in Stage 2 — the four rule-based checks are enough | Mobile screenshots — desktop alone still demos well | The screenshot itself; the demo depends on it                    |
| ---                                                               | ---                                                 | ---                                                              |
| n8n scheduling — run_pipeline.py by hand is fine                  | The suppression list                                | run_pipeline.py itself                                           |
| ---                                                               | ---                                                 | ---                                                              |
| Deploying the dashboard — run it locally for the demo             | Filtering and sorting in the dashboard              | The dashboard rendering a lead end to end                        |
| ---                                                               | ---                                                 | ---                                                              |
| Scoring down from 100 leads to 40                                 | Amna's hand-scoring of 10 drafts                    | Haseeb's quote verification — it is what makes the output honest |
| ---                                                               | ---                                                 | ---                                                              |

**The one thing that must exist on Friday**

One lead, collected from a real source, audited, researched with a verified quote, scored, written up, approved by a human on screen, and visible in the sandbox inbox.

If you have that, the demo works. Everything else — 100 leads, deployment, n8n — makes it better but is not what makes it real.
